meta.title: Band gaps of common photovoltaic materials
meta.description: One representative band gap per material for the lessons, with the range where the gap depends on composition or preparation. 'kind' is direct, indirect or amorphous (no sharp band edge). 'family' picks the technology colour.
meta.license: CC BY 4.0 (compiled by Solar Odyssey from the cited sources)

data.name: Germanium
data.use: Bottom cell and substrate of many space multi-junction cells

data.name: Copper indium gallium selenide
data.use: Thin-film modules on glass or flexible foil
data.note: The gap rises from about 1.04 eV (CuInSe2) to about 1.68 eV (CuGaSe2) as gallium replaces indium. 1.15 eV is our representative value for a gallium-poor mix, not a single measured number.

data.name: Crystalline silicon
data.use: Wafer-based cells in most solar panels
data.note: 1.12 eV (PVEducation gives 1.124 eV) at 300 K. Indirect gap, so absorption near the edge is weak.

data.name: Cadmium telluride
data.note: Room-temperature single-crystal value about 1.51 eV, rounded to 1.50 eV. Values near 1.45–1.5 eV are commonly quoted for polycrystalline films.

data.name: Methylammonium lead iodide perovskite
data.use: The archetypal perovskite absorber; mixed-ion versions tune the gap
data.note: Spectroscopy puts the room-temperature gap at 1.61–1.63 eV; absorption-edge estimates near 1.55–1.6 eV are also common. Mixing ions shifts it widely.

data.name: Hydrogenated amorphous silicon
data.note: Disordered, so there is no sharp band edge; the optical gap is about 1.7 eV and depends on hydrogen content.
